entries.title: Permission denied
entries.explanation:
MINT could not write the output file because the destination folder denies write access. This typically happens when exporting into a system or read-only location (for example a SDCC module install path).

What to do:
  1. Choose a different output folder under your home directory (e.g. ~/exports).
  2. Make sure the destination folder exists and is writable by your user.
  3. If you really need to write to a shared location, ask the administrator to grant write permissions.

patterns: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes
entries.title: Signal arrays have incompatible shapes
entries.explanation:
An expression mixing two or more signals failed because the signal vectors do not have the same length. NumPy refuses to combine arrays of different sizes element-wise.

What to do:
  1. Check the time ranges of the signals involved. If they differ, the time-axis re-alignment is producing different sample counts.
  2. Make sure all signals share the same data source resolution.
  3. Manually align the signals by using the x/y columns and an interpolation expression, or split the calculation per signal.

entries.title: No data sources available
entries.explanation:
MINT could not connect to any UDA or IMAS data source at startup. Without at least one valid data source MINT cannot fetch any data.

What to do:
  1. Check that the environment variable IPLOT_SOURCES_CONFIG points to a valid datasources_def.cfg file.
  2. Confirm that the UDA/IMAS server listed in that file is reachable from your machine.
  3. On SDCC, run `module load MINT` in a fresh shell so the default data sources are configured.

patterns: Processing expression in Variable column is not supported for export
entries.title: Expressions in Variable column cannot be exported
entries.explanation:
Signals declared as expressions (using ${...}) in the Variable column are computed at draw time only. The Export feature exports raw signal data straight from the data source, so derived signals are skipped.

What to do:
  1. If you only need the raw signals, ignore this message: the underlying signals are still exported.
  2. If you need the result of the expression, save the workspace and reproduce the computation downstream from the exported file.

patterns: Custom StartTime/EndTime is not supported for export
entries.title: Per-signal time overrides ignored during export
entries.explanation:
Some signals in the table override the global time range with their own StartTime/EndTime. Export uses only the global time range, so those overrides are ignored.

What to do:
  1. Adjust the global time range to cover the period you want to export.
  2. Or clear the per-signal StartTime/EndTime cells for the signals you want to export.

patterns: Processing in x/y/z columns is not supported for export
entries.title: Custom x/y/z processing ignored during export
entries.explanation:
Some signals use the x, y or z columns to redefine their plotted vectors. Export delivers raw data from the data source and cannot replay these per-signal computations.

What to do:
  1. Export the raw signal and replay the x/y/z transformation in your downstream tool.
  2. Or remove the x/y/z entries before exporting.

patterns: Result of expression=.* is not an instance of
entries.title: Expression result is not a data array
entries.explanation:
The expression you wrote produced a scalar (or unsupported type) instead of a numerical array. MINT cannot plot a single value; it needs a vector of points.

What to do:
  1. Check the expression: did you use np.max(...) where you wanted to keep an array?
  2. Wrap scalar results into an array, e.g. np.max(${a}.data) * np.ones(${a}.data.size).

entries.title: No data available for this signal
entries.explanation:
The data source returned zero points for this signal in the requested time range. The signal exists, but there is no archived data in that interval - or the variable name does not match anything indexed by the server.

What to do:
  1. Widen the time range (or pick a different range where you expect data).
  2. Double-check the variable name for typos. For IMAS data, make sure you used the full path including any [n] indices.
  3. Confirm the data source is the right one (codacuda for ITER plant data, imasuda for IMAS).
  4. If you used Extremities=1, the previous archived sample is shown if available; otherwise the cell stays empty.

patterns: is derived from signals with envelope data
entries.title: Envelope flag missing on derived signal
entries.explanation:
The expression depends on signals that use envelope data (min/avg/max). The result signal must therefore also be marked as envelope, otherwise MINT cannot reconcile the formats.

What to do:
  1. Set the Envelope column to 1 on the derived signal.
  2. Or remove envelope mode on the source signals if you do not need it.
